statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stands at 14 of 100 in the low band, eleven points below the 25 block threshold, while stress is extreme at 84 and confidence high at 89.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The named danger window spans the 12:30 UTC August consumer price report, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC preliminary Michigan release, where the conditional path peaks at WATCH without reaching the block threshold.
headline: NQ trades 29,254-29,258, up about 0.42%, after a marginal new overnight high at 29,268.75, while Brent corrects 2.2% to $105.26 and the two-year eases to 4.56%, leaving tail at 14 and stress extreme at 84 into the 12:30 UTC August consumer price report.
body:
The new evidence this hour is a further marginal extension of the overnight top. NQ trades 29,258.00 on one feed and 29,254.25 on a second, up about 0.42% against a 29,135.25 previous close, with both showing a session high of 29,268.75. That high is roughly twenty points above the 29,248.75 extreme recorded an hour ago, and the 29,040.50 overnight low is unchanged, so the band has widened upward to 228 points with price in its upper reaches. Price is currently some eleven to fourteen points below the high, which means a small retracement is in fact taking place rather than a refusal to pull back.

That distinction is why tail moves only from 13 to 14. Holding near a session extreme is a genuine amplifier, but it is the only one present, and the cross-asset picture has turned less rather than more threatening over the past hour. Brent has corrected about 2.2% to $105.26 after reaching a four-month high of $109.97 overnight, and WTI is down 1.77% to $100.66. The two-year note yield peaked near 4.596%, its highest since July 2024, and has since eased to 4.56%, a decline of roughly three basis points on the session. VIX futures are quoted 1.81% lower against a 17.84 cash close. A slow 0.4% drift higher alongside a correcting energy complex and an easing front end reads as stabilisation after Thursday's selling, not as the persistent one-way structure that overwhelms a mean-reversion basket.

The macro backdrop still justifies extreme stress at 84. The ten-year touched 4.97% in the overnight session, the highest since late 2023, after closing at 4.944%, and the thirty-year reached 5.35%. Thursday's August producer price report printed 0.4% month-over-month, matching consensus, and the combination of that release with oil above $100 has lifted the priced probability of a Federal Reserve rate increase on 16 September to roughly 71 to 72% from about 49% a week earlier. The latest full cash session left semiconductors heavy, with INTC down 5.57%, MU down 4.90%, ARM down 3.80% and AMD down 3.36%, while megacaps were split between AAPL up 3.56% and NVDA down 2.37%. That internal dispersion argues for reduced directional conviction rather than for a higher tail reading.

The session turns on the August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC, which has not been released. Consensus is near 0.4% headline and 0.2% core month-over-month with headline around 3.4% year-over-year. That is the named danger window, extended to 14:30 UTC to cover the 13:30 UTC cash open, where any post-release move is confirmed or rejected, and the 14:00 UTC preliminary Michigan release with its inflation-expectations component. Conditional tail peaks at 23 in the release hour, inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold, because event importance and forecast dispersion belong to stress and confidence until an actual price path can be scored. Confidence rises to 89: the level and day range are confirmed on two independent feeds, and the yield complex, both oil benchmarks, VIX, the release schedule, the consensus and the priced Fed path are all verified on current sources. The only material gap remains that no post-release path yet exists.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 07:00 UTC on 10 September to 06:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 10 and holds a 9 to 11 band through the European morning with the mode recorded as mixed. The single excursion sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the August producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and the window peak of 24 at 13:00 UTC across the cash open. Those two slots are the only ones mapped to WATCH and neither reached the 25 block threshold. Tail then decayed as price discovery stayed orderly, easing to 17 by 14:00 UTC and holding 14 to 19 through the afternoon, with event/whipsaw recorded again at 20:00 and 21:00 UTC around the cash close. From the 22:00 UTC reopen the series settles into a mixed 11 to 15 range, then lifts to 13 with the mode turning trend-up in the final slot as the overnight high was cleared. Stress never left the extreme band, running 80 to 87 across the whole window, and confidence stayed in the high band between 84 and 89. The shape is one event-driven excursion into the watch band followed by a clean decay and a mild overnight upward drift.
outlookSummary: The forward window covers the rest of the 11 September session and ends inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC. Conditional tail starts at 14 on the observed marginal new high, holds 14 through the European morning and rebuilds to 15 and 16 as the release approaches and quoted depth conditionally thins. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price report, inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold, and 22 in the 13:00 UTC slot spanning the cash open where a post-event move is confirmed or rejected. The 14:00 UTC slot carrying the preliminary Michigan release eases to 19 on the assumption that price discovery is orderly by then. The afternoon decays through 17, 15 and 14, lifts to 15 into the final pre-close hour and 18 across the 20:00 UTC weekly close where weekend positioning concentrates, then falls to a 5 to 7 floor for the ten closure hours in which no tradeable price path exists. Stress mirrors that shape, peaking at 92 in the release hour and falling to about 60 inside the closure, while confidence dips to 79 around the cash open because the post-release path cannot be observed in advance. Two slots are mapped to WATCH; none reaches a blocking state.
